evidence_span: indicated for the treatment of adults patients with Obesity with

evidence_records.literal_quote: indicated for the treatment of adults patients with Obesity with
in addition to metformin with or without SGLT2 inhibitors

why: The supplied abridged India PI (LBL p4; 'Updated: Jan 2023', CCDS v6 29 Sep 2022) restricts the indication to adults with obesity and to use in addition to metformin; the claim ('adults with T2DM insufficiently controlled on basal insulin or oral agents') omits both label restrictions. The 'or' is an enumerated qualifier, so each listed subgroup carries label_scope_mismatch (rubric Q1). Scope: this reproduced label only; OCR spans (6 pt print).

why: SoliMix Fig 1B (p5) gives the superiority LS mean difference -0.2 (95% CI -0.4, -0.1), p<0.001 — distinct from the 97.5% noninferiority CI — and the abstract (p1) states reductions of 1.3% and 1.1%; Fig 1B shows them as LS mean ± SE (-1.3 ± 0.1, -1.1 ± 0.1). 'Reduction 1.3' maps to the signed change -1.3 by rule. Background metformin ± SGLT2i is shared by both arms: omitted_context (disclosed).
rubric_rules: 0.5 omitted context (ICH E9(R1) add-on to SoC)

evidence_span: changes from baseline to Week 30 in HbA1c were −1.63% for iGlarLixi, −1.34% for

evidence_records.literal_quote: changes from baseline to Week 30 in HbA1c were −1.63% for iGlarLixi, −1.34% for

why: LixiLan-O p13: LS mean HbA1c changes -1.63% (iGlarLixi) vs -1.34% (iGlar); ratio 1.2164, far outside any reading of ~2x. Table 2 (p29) agrees only at lower precision. The LBL superscript points to LixiLan-L (1.1 vs 0.6 = 1.83x); recorded, not used to rescue the claim.

SoliMix Fig 2 (p6), column 'OR (95% CI)': 42.2% (n=187) vs 31.8% (n=141), adjusted OR 1.65 (1.25, 2.19); the text says the proportion was higher with iGlarLixi. Caveats: exploratory endpoint; adjusted OR (crude 1.5697 is not a substitute); '42.20/31.80' equal the source (presentational flag).
alternatives: cannot_verify if the reviewer requires a confirmatory endpoint

evidence_span: Mean body weight decreased by 0.7 kg with iGlarLixi and increased by

evidence_records.literal_quote: Mean body weight decreased by 0.7 kg with iGlarLixi and increased by

why: The abstract (raster, OCR) reports a 0.7 kg decrease vs a 0.7 kg increase with iGlar. 'Weight neutral' is a substantive no-meaningful-change claim that needs a prespecified margin or equivalence analysis; none is given (and no author statement). Weight loss, no gain, non-significance and equivalence are different assertions.
alternatives: overstated if the reviewer reads the front panel as generalising beyond LixiLan-L

why: SoliMix Fig 3A (p7): level 2 hypoglycaemia 6.3% (n=28) iGlarLixi vs 12.9% (n=57) BIAsp 30 (arms from layout: n=442 legend row above n=441), OR 0.45 (95% CI 0.28, 0.73). Non-scored panel finding: the LBL's '55% lower risk' is a relative odds reduction; count-based RR is 0.4901.

evidence_records.literal_quote: All P values are reported as nominal P values
0.7 kg with iGlar (1.4 kg difference, P < 0.0001)

why: The claim names three LBL panels, so their numbers are in scope. Each analysis shows a weight benefit (LixiLan-L -0.7 vs +0.7 kg at 30 wk; SoliMix -0.7 vs +1.2 kg at 26 wk; Tabák -0.62 vs +0.70 kg at 24 vs 26 wk), but the SoliMix panel's p<0.0001 is not established by the paper's P<0.001, and the LixiLan-L panel's n=365/366 and ±0.2 kg are not in the abstract. No contradiction. Caveats: post hoc PSM with nominal P (disclosed); shared participants (not three independent replications).
alternatives: overstated under a strict design reading
